paragraphs: A certain king was surrounded by a huge crowd of courtiers. Every single one of them claimed he would gladly die for his master and that he was the most sincere person who had ever lived.

One day a sannyasin, a wandering monk, visited the court. The king proudly told him that no king in history had ever had such devoted courtiers. The monk smiled and said he did not believe it. Test them if you like, said the king.

So the sannyasin announced that he would perform a great sacrifice to give the king a long reign. There was one condition. A small tank would be built, and during the dark of night each courtier was to come and pour a pitcher of milk into it.

The king laughed. Was that all? He called his courtiers and explained the plan, and they all agreed with great enthusiasm. That night, in the darkness, each of them came quietly and emptied his pitcher into the tank.

At sunrise the tank was full, but of plain water. When the courtiers were gathered and questioned, the truth came out. Every one of them had thought the same thing: with so much milk going in, nobody would notice one pitcher of water. Swamiji added that most of us do our share of work in exactly the same way.
learn: In group projects, team chores or community work, it is tempting to think your small shortcut will get lost in everyone else's effort. But if everyone thinks that way, the whole thing collapses. Do your part honestly, as if yours were the only pitcher.
